instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F/190°C with a rack in the middle. Butter a 9 by 13 inch baking dish.
Trim the leeks, cut off the dark green tops and halve them lengthwise. Slice them thinly, then rinse the slices in a bowl of cold water and drain them well. Shred the Gruyere.
Set a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the butter and the leeks with 1/2 tsp of the salt and the thyme. Cook for 7 minutes, stirring often, until soft and starting to brown.

While the leeks cook, whisk the cornstarch with 1/4 cup of the milk in a large bowl until smooth. Add the eggs, the rest of the milk, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp of the pepper and the nutmeg and whisk until smooth.
Spread the leeks in the baking dish in an even layer and scatter the Gruyere over them. Pour the custard over the leeks.
Bake for 22 minutes, until the top is lightly golden and the center is set. It should barely jiggle when you shake the dish.
Let it stand for 4 minutes. Meanwhile, squeeze the lemon over the greens, add the olive oil, a pinch of salt and the remaining 1/4 tsp pepper and toss.
Taste a bit of the quiche. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt to the salad greens or the slice.
Cut the quiche into squares and serve with the salad.
method_notes: The crustless leek and Gruyere sources agree on leeks cooked in butter or oil first, a custard of eggs and milk, Gruyere on top and a bake at 350°F. They differ on cream against milk, cornstarch against none, and the size of the dish. This follows the cornstarch version, bakes it in a wide 9 by 13 dish at 375°F so it sets in about 22 minutes, and uses no flour.
